q: What is expert judgment?
options: A decision made only by the project manager
Judgment based on expertise in an application area, discipline or industry, from any person or group with specialized knowledge
A vote taken by the whole team
explanation: Expert judgment may be provided by any group or person with specialized education, knowledge, skill, experience or training.

q: The team needs to produce a large number of ideas in a short time, without judging them at first. Which technique fits?
explanation: Brainstorming is used to identify a list of ideas in a short period of time, in a group led by a facilitator.

q: A project needs the opinions of 3,000 users located in six countries, and needs them quickly. Which technique is most suitable?
explanation: Questionnaires and surveys collect information quickly from a large number of respondents, and suit geographically dispersed audiences.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Questionnaires and surveys

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Questionnaires and surveys

q: The team compares its processes with those of leading organizations to find best practices and ideas for improvement. Which technique is this?
explanation: Benchmarking compares actual or planned products, processes and practices with those of comparable organizations to identify best practices.

q: The same defect keeps reappearing after each repair. Which technique should the team use?
explanation: Root cause analysis determines the basic underlying reason for a variance, defect or risk. When the root causes are removed, the problem does not recur.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Root cause analysis

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Root cause analysis

q: The project manager compares actual performance with the baseline to determine the size and cause of the difference. Which technique is this?
explanation: Variance analysis determines the cause and degree of difference between the baseline and actual performance.

q: Using the results of the last six months, the project manager forecasts whether the project will stay within budget. Which technique is this?
explanation: Trend analysis uses mathematical models to forecast future outcomes based on historical results. It warns in advance if problems are likely.

q: The team must select one of several possible approaches for doing the work. Which data analysis technique evaluates the options?
explanation: Alternative analysis evaluates identified options in order to select the options or approaches to use when performing the work of the project.

q: After a workshop, the team has 90 ideas on sticky notes and wants to sort them into groups for review. Which tool fits?
explanation: An affinity diagram shows large numbers of ideas classified into groups for review and analysis.

q: Twelve people vote on a proposal and seven support it. Which decision-making method produced the decision?
explanation: A majority is support from more than 50% of the group. Seven of twelve is 58%.

q: Ten people vote on three options. The results are 4, 3 and 3, and the option with 4 votes is selected. Which method is this?
explanation: With plurality the largest block decides even though a majority (more than 50%, here at least 6) is not achieved.

q: A team scores three suppliers against weighted criteria such as price, experience and delivery time, and ranks them by total score. Which technique is this?
options: Plurality voting by show of hands
explanation: Multicriteria decision analysis uses a decision matrix: criteria are weighted and applied to all alternatives to give each a score, and the alternatives are ranked.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Multicriteria decision analysis

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Multicriteria decision analysis

q: What does the "M" in the MoSCoW prioritization method stand for?
explanation: MoSCoW stands for must have, should have, could have and will not have. It is used to prioritize requirements.

q: Which skill is the ability to guide a group event to a successful decision or conclusion, ensuring that everyone participates and all contributions are considered?
explanation: Facilitation is the ability to effectively guide a group event to a successful decision, solution or conclusion.

q: What is a project management information system (PMIS)?
options: An information system of tools used to gather, integrate and disseminate the outputs of project management processes
explanation: A PMIS gives access to tools such as scheduling software, work authorization, configuration management and information distribution systems.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Project management information system (PMIS)

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Project management information system (PMIS)

q: A team keeps a large board on the wall, updated by hand, showing the status of every task so that anyone walking by can see it. What is this called?
explanation: An information radiator is a visible, physical display that shares information with the organization. It is easy to update and often maintained by hand.

q: What does a burndown chart show?
options: The work completed toward a milestone
The work remaining against the time left in a timebox
explanation: A burndown chart shows the work remaining versus the time left in a timebox. A burnup chart shows the work completed toward a milestone.

q: In a brief daily meeting, team members say what they did yesterday, what they will do today and what is blocking them. What is this meeting called?
explanation: A daily coordination meeting reviews progress from the previous day, declares intentions for the current day and highlights obstacles.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Daily coordination meeting

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Daily coordination meeting

q: What is the main purpose of a retrospective?
options: To demonstrate the product to the customer
To explore how the team worked and how to improve the process
explanation: A retrospective is a regular workshop in which participants explore their work and results in order to improve both the process and the product.

q: Which of the following is good meeting management practice?
options: Distributing an agenda with the objectives, and recording actions with the person responsible
Letting the meeting run until all topics are exhausted
explanation: Good practice includes preparing and distributing the agenda, starting and finishing on time, inviting the appropriate participants, staying on topic and recording all actions with owners.

q: In team discussions one senior person always speaks first and the others simply agree. Which approach would best reduce this effect?
options: Collecting each person's input individually before discussion, or revealing all votes at the same time
Removing the senior person from the project
explanation: Structured methods such as the nominal group technique gather everyone's input before discussion, and simultaneous voting minimizes groupthink and the influence of dominant members.

q: Which technique involves acknowledging, clarifying and confirming what the other person says, in order to reduce misunderstanding?
explanation: Active listening uses techniques such as acknowledging, clarifying and confirming to reduce misunderstandings, especially in cross-cultural settings.
